title: Europe · breeds of the north and the islands
blurb: Britain, France, Russia and Scandinavia: dense shorthairs, forest longhairs and the island mutations that gave the rex and the Manx.

items.d: Round, dense-coated and calm; Britain's native shorthair and one of the oldest recognised breeds.
The blue-grey French cat of the monasteries, quiet, stocky and famously a good mouser.
Silver-tipped blue coat, green eyes and a reserved manner; said to have come from Arkhangelsk.
The skogkatt of Norway: a double coat, a strong climber and a saga name to match.
Russia's forest cat, with a triple coat and an oily top layer that sheds snow.
The tailless cat of the Isle of Man, with a rounded rump and a hopping gait.
The folded-ear cat of Scotland, 1961, with a round head and an owl-like look.
A short, wavy coat and huge ears, from a curly kitten found in Devon in 1959.
